parts.gloss: to those who do not steal

words.gloss: to those who do not steal

literal: To those who steal, the abode of life will be lost; to those who do not steal, the celestial world will not be denied.
translation: For those who steal, even their very life-abode will be lost; but for those who do not steal, the celestial world of the gods will never be denied.
modern: திருடுபவர்களுக்கு உடம்பாகிய உயிர்நிலை தவறிப்போகும்; திருடாதவர்களுக்குத் தேவர் உலகம் தவறாமல் கிடைக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the ultimate spiritual and physical fates of those who steal and those who practice non-stealing. For the thief, even the basic right to a proper physical existence or the preservation of their life (உயிர்நிலை) is lost due to their actions. In contrast, for those who strictly avoid theft, the ultimate celestial realm of the gods (புத்தேள் உலகு) is guaranteed and will never be withheld from them. The poet uses the contrast between losing one's earthly station and gaining the highest heavenly world to emphasize the gravity of non-stealing.
